title: phegopteris straminea
intro: Phegopteris straminea, commonly known as the golden polypody fern, is a species of fern that belongs to the family Dryopteridaceae. This plant is traditionally used in folk medicine for its health benefits, which include treating various ailments such as fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions. The therapeutic actions of Phegopteris straminea are attributed to its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, which help to soothe and protect the skin and mucous membranes. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, terpenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
